Observations from a first pass on oakbridge_error_sample.log.txt:
- I see a pattern of truncated header blocks and repeated partial-header sequences that line up with the timestamps of increased 5xx.
- The client connection (identified by session id) shows fragmented meta headers across multiple frames — frames arrive out-of-order from the SDK side in about ~0.4% of connections under burst load in this sample.
- Our runtime normally reassembles headers, but if a fragment sequence is missing or duplicated it can trigger a retry loop that both raises token latency and reduces throughput because of backpressure.

Likely root cause: an edge-case in SDK v1.6.2's streaming encoder that emits adjacent header fragments without the expected continuation flag when it hits a particular buffer boundary under high concurrency. This was not present in our internal low-concurrency tests.

Attached: sdk_parser_diff.patch (proposed fix that forces explicit fragment markers and adds a small coalescing delay when buffer boundaries align). I can build a quick canary SDK in ~3 hours.

Temporary mitigation options (pick one):
- Have OakBridge enable request-level retry suppression for the affected routes (low-risk, reduces retries).
- Route OakBridge traffic to a dedicated pool with slightly higher reassembly timeout (puts load on Dedicated capacity).
- Deploy a quick SDK patch in canary.

I'll start a reproducer against our local harness now (linking results to the Drive folder).

—Ben
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

Patricia — thanks for the extra traces and permission to canary. Summary and immediate plan:

Summary of findings (TL;DR):
- Root cause hypothesis: SDK v1.6.2 streaming encoder exposes a fragmentation edge-case under high concurrent sessions that can emit header fragments without explicit continuation markers. The runtime's reassembler tolerates most cases but under the observed pattern it enters a retry/backpressure loop, causing p99 latency and throughput drop.

Immediate mitigation we will execute (timeline):
1) Ben will push a patched SDK build (v1.6.3-canary) to our internal canary repo in ~3 hours and provide OakBridge a private artifact URL. (ETA: Sun 21:45 PDT)
2) OakBridge to run canary against 1% traffic for checkout routes for 2 hours. Redwood will monitor ingress reassembly error counts and token latency in real-time. (ETA: Mon 00:30 PDT — need your confirmation for start window.)
3) If canary looks good, we coordinate a staged rollout to 25%/50%/100% across a 6-hour window and publish a short advisory.
4) If canary fails, we will apply the temporary mitigation of routing OakBridge to a dedicated pool with extended reassembly timeout until a full fix is rolled.

Org escalation: I have briefed Lauren and Product; execs are on standby for customer outreach. We'll aim to have a public post-mortem within 72 hours from incident close.

Patricia — can you confirm you can do the 1% canary at the proposed window tonight (00:30 PDT) and that you have an engineer available for a quick 15-min check-in? Also confirm your acceptance of the temporary routing plan if the canary has issues.
